A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same APUB research and contain readable text, equations, six figures, and complete Appendices A and B. The material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original Monte Carlo results in Example 2.5 and product-mix and multi-product newsvendor experiments in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original simulations and optimization experiments, including the results in Figures 1–6.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 introduces bootstrap multiplicity weights and shared recourse variables. The LP changes from MN recourse blocks in v1 Equation (14) to N blocks in v3 Equation (16). This is a computational refinement of the retained APUB objective and bootstrap approach.

E1.justification: Both versions use the Gamma simulation, product-mix problems with fixed and random recourse, and ten-product newsvendor problems with original and noise-added demand. Appendix B's data-generation parameters are identical.

E2.justification: Example 2.5 retains Efron's and standard large-sample upper bounds. The fixed-recourse experiment retains SAA-M and WassDRO, while the random-recourse and newsvendor experiments retain their SAA-M comparisons.

E3.justification: Data generation, sample sizes, confidence-level and Wasserstein-radius sweeps, out-of-sample evaluation, and coverage metrics are retained. Both versions use M = 2000 bootstrap samples for the subsequent Section 5.1 experiments; the revised LP does not introduce a different evaluation design.

E4.justification: Both retain bootstrap convergence analysis, sensitivity to sample size and confidence level, random-recourse and noise comparisons, and the newsvendor order-quantity analysis. No additional ablation or robustness analysis appears.

E5.justification: Both report 10 independent convergence simulations, 1000 Monte Carlo replications for the performance comparison, and means with 10th–90th percentile ranges. Run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 1–6 contain identical plotted results, and the numerical findings in the experimental text are retained. For example, Section 5.3.2 reports the same solution-distance values of 7.89, 3.99, and 3.36. No new runtime or performance results accompany the reformulation.

T1.justification: Section 2.1 changes the VaR definition from strict inequalities to the non-strict quantile convention. Section 4.2 adds a formal finite-objective decision domain and states relatively complete recourse. The principal asymptotic theorems and Appendix A remain unchanged; most other mathematical edits clarify notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about APUB, asymptotic correctness and consistency, interpretability, reduced conservatism, and bootstrap tractability.

C2.justification: v3 Section 4.2 explicitly discusses relatively complete recourse and explains excluding decisions without feasible recourse actions. The experimental interpretations, cost-versus-coverage tradeoff, and limitation under severe sample scarcity are otherwise unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 specifies how to construct multiplicity weights by counting each original observation's bootstrap occurrences and gives the corresponding compact LP indexing. Other experimental details and Appendix B's numerical inputs remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography and positioning relative to bootstrap inference, CVaR, and DRO are unchanged. Dantzig remains cited despite one occurrence becoming an unresolved marker; no identifiable cited work is added or removed.

P1.justification: Section 4 gains separate convergence and practical-reformulation subsections, notation explanations expand, and acknowledgments are added. Most prose remains intact. Citation formatting changes also introduce unresolved markers in Sections 4.2 and 5.1.

P2.justification: The six figures retain their graphics, axes, legends, and captions. Figure 2 is repositioned, Figures 4 and 5 move to later pages, and Figure 6 no longer interrupts the conclusion. The overall layout remains similar.

improvement.justification: v3 makes the solution approach more practical through the compact weighted LP and more explicit recourse conditions. These are useful, localized gains. The empirical evidence and main guarantees remain unchanged, no runtime validation is added, and two unresolved citation markers reduce polish.
